I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (that a different family member pays for) and I wanted him to have his own, so I made it clear they can keep his other one and this one is STRICTLY for him. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my mom she's a bad mother. Let me start by understanding the situation better. From what I remember, a while back, I made my mom upset because of a couple of things I said while we were out together. She was talking about how she doesn't believe in doctors, and my siblings literally begged her to take them, but she still put it off as long as possible. I told her that's not okay because she did that to me, and I nearly died. I was hospitalized for weeks and had to spend several months on bed rest recovering. I said that if she keeps doing that, one of us might die someday because of her. She didn't take it well but ended up dropping it and brushing it off as no big deal. Later, she asked me to grab her a drink, and when I asked her what she wanted, she said, "Well, you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" I told her no, I don't know what she likes because my grandparents raised me, so I still don't know anything about her. She got upset and started crying, saying, "What's your problem? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean; I was just saying it's not cool not to take your kid to the doctor and that I don't know anything about her since I didn't grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again a few weeks later. Then, I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (which a different family member pays for), and I wanted him to have his own. I made it clear they can keep his other one, and this one is STRICTLY for him. But I found out they've been taking and using this one too. When I saw her, I told her seriously, I don't want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what she's doing, but I will take it back if she doesn't stop stealing it from him. I said it's HIS phone that I'M paying for, not hers. It's not her's to touch. It's already bad enough that she keeps all his work money, at least don't touch his phone. She got upset and started yelling and crying, saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well, to be honest, she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown, started sobbing, and said, "Well fine, I don't need you in my life anyway," and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. So, AITA? (Am I the Asshole?) Hmm, okay, so I need to think about whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my mom she's a bad mother. Let me break this down. First, I need to consider the context. My mom has a history of not taking her kids to the doctor, which has had serious consequences for me. I nearly died because of her actions. That's a significant issue. She didn't take it seriously when I confronted her about it, which might indicate a pattern of behavior. Then, when she asked me to get her a drink, she made a comment implying I should know her preferences because she raised me. But since my grandparents raised me, I don't have that knowledge. My response was honest but perhaps harsh. She took it as me being mean and trying to make her look bad. Later, regarding the phone, she continued taking my brother's phone, which I bought for him. I set boundaries, but she reacted strongly, leading me to tell her she's a bad mother. She left, and now my family is advising me not to treat her that way. So, is it right or wrong for me to tell her she's a bad mother? I think it's important to consider the impact of my words. While my mom's actions have been harmful, calling her a bad mother is a strong statement. It can hurt her feelings and damage our relationship further. However, I also need to consider my own well-being and the need to set boundaries. Maybe there's a better way to communicate my concerns without labeling her. It's possible that she has her own issues or struggles that contribute to her behavior. Addressing the specific actions rather than her character might be more constructive. On the other hand, if her behavior is consistently harmful, it's important to stand up for myself and my brother. Setting boundaries is necessary, but the way I communicate it can make a difference. Using "I" statements and focusing on how her actions affect me rather than labeling her might be more effective. In conclusion, while my mom's behavior is concerning, calling her a bad mother might not be the best approach. It's better to address the specific issues and set boundaries in a way that respects both our feelings and promotes healthier communication.
